name: Swiss Standard German (Hochdeutsch)
notes: Swiss Standard German (Schweizer Hochdeutsch). NO glottal stop /ʔ/ — absent from Swiss German phonology. /r/ = alveolar trill [r] (vs. Standard German uvular [ʀ]). Geminate consonants preserved as distinct (Alemannic feature). Swiss German DIALECTS (Schweizerdeutsch) are Alemannic and much more divergent than Swiss Standard German; they are modelled separately by de-x-alemannic, which carries ISO 639-3 gsw and the Alemannic grapheme divergences. Source: König & van der Auwera (1994). Stress exemption: Swiss Standard German stress broadly follows German root-initial stress, but pronunciation (and hence effective stress placement in loanwords/compounds) varies materially across the Swiss German dialect continuum feeding this register; no single spelling-predictable rule is declared. Source: Christen, Helen (1998), Dialekt im Alltag, on regional variation feeding Swiss Standard German usage; Wiese, Richard (1996), The Phonology of German.
